brief:
The UK government defended its designation of Palestine Action as a terrorist organisation before the Supreme Court on Thursday, arguing the group is not merely a non-violent protest movement, Al-Monitor reported. A government lawyer presented the case to Britain's highest court as the organisation challenges the ban.

Palestine Action has contested the classification, asserting it engages in non-violent activism. The legal proceedings centre on whether the government's terrorist designation meets legal standards for such designations in the UK.
dek: A UK government lawyer on Thursday defended before Britain's highest court the banning of Palestine Action as a "terrorist" organisation, insisting that it was not a "non-violent protest group".
title: UK defends banning Palestine Action as terrorist group in court
